newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Anti-Taleban alliance hopeful general will rejoin.
newsitem.headline: Anti-Taleban alliance hopeful general will rejoin.

text.p: The anti-Taleban grouping in north Afghanistan said on Thursday it was more confident that General Abdul Malik, who apparently mutinied to join the purist Islamic Taleban, can be persuaded to return to the alliance.

The opposition said Malik mutinied in protest against alliance leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum rather than in support of the Taleban. It is negotiating with Malik to try to get him to rejoin the opposition alliance.

"Today the negotiations went better, Malik sent some elders to see Dostum. I am more confident than last night." opposition spokesman Dr Abdullah told Reuters by satellite telephone from northern Afghanistan.

The opposition alliance was thrown into disarray and its front line crumbled when Malik apparently turned against Dostum last Monday. Malik was pivotal in the defence of the opposition's western front line with the Taleban.
But there remains uncertainty as to how much the territory the Taleban have captured and how much is still under the control of the opposition.

Abdullah said there had been no clashes between Malik's forces and those of Dostum on the front line close to the border of Jawzjan and Faryab provinces. Malik was governor of Faryab province at the time of the mutiny.
"There were no clashes on the front line today and that is a good sign," he said.
The Taleban say Malik and his forces have been absorbed into their ranks and that the whole of the provinces of Faryab and Sar-i-Pul are under their control.
There was no independent verification of Abdullah's comments.

Taleban forces and those of Hezb-i-Wahadat, a mainly Shi'ite group that is a member of the opposition alliance, were battling on Wednesday night in the district of Sheikh Ali, close to the strategic Shiber Pass in central Afghanistan, he said.
The pass leads into the Bamiyan valley and from there to the north of the country.

"Last night the Taleban attacked in Sheikh Ali, but their attack was pushed back. They took some losses and retreated." he said. The Taleban were unavailable for comment on the situation in Sheikh Ali.
